title: Lenses — 40 MCQs
description: Properties of spherical lenses, the relation between object distance, image distance and focal length of a convex lens, visual angle and angular magnification, the lens maker's formula and its use in finding focal length, and the combined focal length of two thin lenses in contact.

questions.q: For a spherical lens, the relation between the object distance u, the image distance v and the focal length f (real-is-positive convention) is
questions.explanation: The thin lens formula is 1/u + 1/v = 1/f, where u, v and f are all measured from the optical centre of the lens.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about a convex lens is correct?
options: It is a converging lens and its focal length is taken as positive
It is a converging lens and its focal length is taken as negative
It is a diverging lens and its focal length is taken as positive
It always forms a virtual image of a real object
questions.explanation: A convex lens is thicker at the middle, so it converges a parallel beam of light to a real focus; by the real-is-positive convention its focal length is positive.

questions.q: The linear magnification m produced by a lens is given by
questions.explanation: Magnification is the ratio of the image height to the object height, and it also equals −v/u; a negative value shows that the image is real and inverted.

questions.q: The angular magnification of an optical instrument is defined as the ratio of
options: the size of the image to the size of the object
the focal length of the lens to the object distance
the angle subtended at the eye by the image to the angle subtended at the eye by the object when viewed directly
the image distance to the object distance
questions.explanation: Angular magnification compares the visual angle produced by the image with the visual angle subtended by the object itself, both measured at the eye.

questions.q: The visual angle of an object at the eye is the angle
options: subtended by the object at the eye, and a larger visual angle makes the object appear larger
subtended by the image at the principal focus
between the incident ray and the emergent ray through a lens
between the two ends of the object and the optical centre of a lens
questions.explanation: The apparent size of an object depends on the visual angle it subtends at the eye; optical instruments increase this angle, thereby magnifying the object.

questions.q: Lens maker's formula for a thin lens of refractive index n and radii of curvature R₁ and R₂ is
questions.explanation: Lens maker's formula is 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂), which shows that the focal length depends on the material of the lens and on the curvature of its two surfaces.

questions.q: When two thin lenses of focal lengths f₁ and f₂ are placed in contact, the focal length F of the combination is given by
questions.explanation: The powers of lenses in contact add, so P = P₁ + P₂, which in terms of focal lengths gives 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂.

questions.q: The power of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length in metres, and its SI unit is
questions.explanation: P = 1/f with f in metres, so the unit of power is m⁻¹, which is called the dioptre; a convex lens has positive power and a concave lens negative power.

questions.q: The image formed by a concave lens of a real object placed anywhere in front of it is always
options: real, erect and of the same size
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges the refracted rays, so the image is always virtual, erect and smaller than the object, and it lies on the same side as the object.

questions.q: The power of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm is
questions.explanation: P = 1/f = 1/0.20 m = 5 dioptre.

questions.q: An object is placed 15 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The image is formed at a distance of
options: 30 cm on the same side as the object
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so v = +30 cm; the image is real and is formed on the other side of the lens.

questions.q: An object is placed 20 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The magnification produced is
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 20 × 10/10 = 20 cm, so m = −v/u = −20/20 = −1; the image is real, inverted and of the same size.

questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. The image distance is
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = (3 − 2)/60 = 1/60, so v = 60 cm, a real image on the other side of the lens.

questions.q: An object is placed only 5 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The image is formed
options: 5 cm from the lens on the same side
10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object
10 cm from the lens on the other side
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 5 × 10/(5 − 10) = −10 cm; the negative sign shows a virtual image 10 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.

questions.q: An object is placed 10 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The image formed is
options: virtual, 6 cm from the lens on the same side
real, 25 cm from the lens on the other side
virtual, 30 cm from the lens on the same side as the object
real, 30 cm from the lens on the other side
questions.explanation: v = 10 × 15/(10 − 15) = −30 cm, so the image is virtual, erect and magnified three times, formed on the same side as the object.

questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. The image is formed at a distance of
options: 12 cm from the lens on the other side
20 cm from the lens on the other side
12 cm from the lens on the same side as the object
60 cm from the lens on the same side
questions.explanation: For a concave lens f = −20 cm, so v = u f/(u − f) = 30 × (−20)/(30 + 20) = −12 cm; the image is virtual and lies 12 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.

questions.q: Two thin convex lenses of focal length 20 cm each are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is
Two thin convex lenses of focal lengths 20 cm and 30 cm are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is
questions.explanation: 1/F = 1/20 + 1/30 = (3 + 2)/60 = 1/12, so F = 12 cm, which is smaller than either focal length.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with another lens and the combination has a focal length of 60 cm. The focal length of the second lens is
questions.explanation: 1/f₂ = 1/F − 1/f₁ = 1/60 − 1/20 = −2/60 = −1/30, so f₂ = −30 cm; the second lens is concave.

questions.q: Two thin lenses of focal lengths 10 cm and 15 cm are placed in contact. The power of the combination is
A convex lens of focal length 30 cm is placed in contact with a second lens, and the combination behaves as a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. The second lens is
options: a convex lens of focal length 45 cm
a concave lens of focal length 10 cm
a concave lens of focal length 45 cm
a convex lens of focal length 10 cm
questions.explanation: 1/f₂ = 1/F − 1/f₁ = −1/15 − 1/30 = −1/10, so f₂ = −10 cm; the second lens is concave with focal length 10 cm.

questions.q: The power of a concave lens of focal length 50 cm is
questions.explanation: f = −50 cm = −0.5 m, so P = 1/f = −2 dioptre.

questions.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 5 cm is used to view an object with the image at the least distance of distinct vision (25 cm). The angular magnification is
questions.explanation: M = 1 + D/f = 1 + 25/5 = 6, where D = 25 cm is the least distance of distinct vision.

questions.q: A simple microscope of focal length 10 cm forms the image at the near point, 25 cm from the eye. Its magnifying power is
questions.explanation: M = 1 + D/f = 1 + 25/10 = 3.5 when the image is at the near point; for the image at infinity M = D/f = 25/10 = 2.5.

questions.q: An object is placed 12 cm from a convex lens of focal length 8 cm. The image is formed at a distance of
options: 24 cm on the same side as the object
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24, so v = 24 cm; the image is real, inverted and twice as large as the object.

questions.q: A biconvex lens is made of glass of refractive index 1.6 and both its surfaces have a radius of curvature of 24 cm. Its focal length is
A plano-convex lens is made of glass of refractive index 1.5 and the curved surface has a radius of curvature of 12 cm. Its focal length is
A convex lens of focal length 10 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. The focal length of the combination is
options: 30 cm, and it behaves as a convex lens
6 cm, and it behaves as a convex lens
25 cm, and it behaves as a concave lens
30 cm, and it behaves as a concave lens
questions.explanation: 1/F = 1/10 + 1/(−15) = 1/30, so F = +30 cm; the combination is still converging because the convex lens is the more powerful.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 12 cm is placed in contact with a convex lens of focal length 4 cm. The focal length of the combination is
questions.explanation: 1/F = 1/12 + 1/4 = (1 + 3)/12 = 1/3, so F = 3 cm; the combination is much more powerful than either lens alone.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. The combination has a focal length of
questions.explanation: 1/F = 1/20 + 1/(−30) = (3 − 2)/60 = 1/60, so F = +60 cm, i.e. the combination behaves as a weak convex lens.

questions.q: A convex lens forms a real image three times as large as the object placed 20 cm in front of it. The focal length of the lens is
questions.explanation: For a real image m = −3, so v = 3u = 60 cm. Then 1/f = 1/u + 1/v = 1/20 + 1/60 = 4/60 = 1/15, giving f = 15 cm.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm forms a real image twice as large as the object. The object distance is
questions.explanation: For a real image m = −2, so v = 2u. Then 1/u + 1/(2u) = 1/15 gives 3/(2u) = 1/15, so u = 22.5 cm and v = 45 cm.

questions.q: A convex lens of power +5 D is placed in contact with a concave lens of power −3 D. The focal length of the combination is
questions.explanation: P = P₁ + P₂ = +5 − 3 = +2 D, so F = 1/P = 1/2 m = 50 cm; the combination behaves as a convex lens.

questions.q: A glass lens (n = 1.5) has a focal length of 20 cm in air. When it is completely immersed in water (n = 1.33), its focal length becomes about
questions.explanation: In air, 1/f = (1.5 − 1)K = 1/20, so K = 0.1 cm⁻¹. In water, 1/f_w = (1.5/1.33 − 1) × 0.1 = 0.0128 cm⁻¹, giving f_w ≈ 78 cm; the lens becomes much weaker in water.

questions.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 2.5 cm is used with the image at the least distance of distinct vision (25 cm). The angular magnification is
questions.explanation: M = 1 + D/f = 1 + 25/2.5 = 11; if instead the image were at infinity the magnification would be only 25/2.5 = 10.

questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a concave lens of focal length 15 cm. The magnification of the image is
questions.explanation: v = u f/(u − f) = 30 × (−15)/(30 + 15) = −10 cm, so m = −v/u = +10/30 = +1/3; the image is virtual, erect and one-third the size of the object.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. The combination behaves as
options: a concave lens of focal length 10 cm
a convex lens of focal length 40 cm
a convex lens of focal length 10 cm
a plane glass plate of infinite focal length
questions.explanation: 1/F = 1/20 + 1/(−20) = 0, so F is infinite; the two equal and opposite powers cancel and the combination neither converges nor diverges a beam.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 40 cm is combined with another lens so that the combination behaves as a concave lens of focal length 40 cm. The second lens is
options: a concave lens of focal length 40 cm
a concave lens of focal length 80 cm
a convex lens of focal length 20 cm
a concave lens of focal length 20 cm
questions.explanation: 1/f₂ = 1/F − 1/f₁ = −1/40 − 1/40 = −1/20, so f₂ = −20 cm, i.e. a concave lens of focal length 20 cm.

questions.q: A lens is made of glass of refractive index 1.5 with radii of curvature R₁ = 10 cm and R₂ = −15 cm. Its focal length is
A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms a virtual image twice as large as the object. The object distance is
questions.explanation: For a virtual, erect image m = +2, so v = −2u. Then 1/u + 1/(−2u) = 1/10 gives 1/(2u) = 1/10, so u = 5 cm, i.e. the object lies between the lens and its focus.
